title: Coordinate graded derivations on finite connected signed bialgebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A^n$ a finite-dimensional graded associative unital $k$-algebra, with $A^0=k\cdot1$, $1\ne0$, and $ab=(-1)^{ij}ba$ for homogeneous $a\in A^i,b\in A^j$. Suppose a degree-preserving coassociative unital algebra map $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_kA$ is given, where $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg b\deg c}ac\otimes bd$, and the projection $\varepsilon:A\to A^0=k$ satisfies both counit identities. Put $I=\bigoplus_{n>0}A^n$, and let $I^2$ be the span of products of two elements of $I$. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ be positive-degree homogeneous elements, of degrees $d_1,\ldots,d_s$, whose classes form a $k$-basis of $I/I^2$. For every $i$ there is a $k$-linear map $\partial_i:A\to A$ of degree $-d_i$, with $\partial_i(1)=0$, $\partial_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}\cdot1$, and $\partial_i(ab)=\partial_i(a)b+(-1)^{d_i\deg a}a\partial_i(b)$ for homogeneous $a,b$. Here a negative graded component is zero. No perfectness, cocommutativity, or characteristic restriction is required.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, first sentence of the proof (Borel structure input); agent-written graded invariant-derivation prerequisite, not a lemma stated in Milne.

proof.text: The grading makes $I^2$ a graded subspace: expand both factors of each product into their homogeneous components. Thus $Q=I/I^2$ is graded and the given classes $\bar x_j$ are a homogeneous basis. Let $\lambda_i:Q\to k$ extract the coefficient of $\bar x_i$, and put $\phi_i(a)=\lambda_i([a-\varepsilon(a)1])$. This is $k$-linear, vanishes on $1$ and $I^2$, and satisfies $\phi_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}$. It vanishes on $A^n$ for $n\ne d_i$: in a homogeneous-basis expansion of a degree-$n$ class all coefficients of other degrees vanish. Expanding $a=\varepsilon(a)1+u$, $b=\varepsilon(b)1+v$, with $u,v\in I$, gives $\phi_i(ab)=\phi_i(a)\varepsilon(b)+\varepsilon(a)\phi_i(b)$ since $uv\in I^2$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text: Use the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with base ring $k$ and $M=N=P=A$, for the bilinear map $(u,v)\mapsto\phi_i(u)v$. It gives a well-defined linear contraction $C_i:A\otimes_kA\to A$, $C_i(u\otimes v)=\phi_i(u)v$. Define $D_i=C_i\Delta$. If $a\in A^n$, write $\Delta(a)$ as a finite sum of homogeneous simple tensors $a_1\otimes a_2$ with $\deg a_1+\deg a_2=n$; such tensors span each graded component by the tensor-product presentation. Only terms with $\deg a_1=d_i$ survive contraction. Consequently $D_i(A^n)\subseteq A^{n-d_i}$, with zero output when $n<d_i$, and $D_i(1)=C_i(1\otimes1)=0$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text:
For homogeneous $a,b$, expand $\Delta(a)=\sum a_1\otimes a_2$, $\Delta(b)=\sum b_1\otimes b_2$ homogeneously. The signed product and the identity for $\phi_i$ give
$$D_i(ab)=\sum(-1)^{\deg a_2\deg b_1}\bigl(\phi_i(a_1)\varepsilon(b_1)+\varepsilon(a_1)\phi_i(b_1)\bigr)a_2b_2.$$
In the first summand $\varepsilon(b_1)\ne0$ forces $\deg b_1=0$, so its sign is $1$. In the second, a nonzero scalar requires $\deg a_1=0$ and $\deg b_1=d_i$, so its sign is $(-1)^{d_i\deg a}$. Using $\sum\varepsilon(b_1)b_2=b$ and $\sum\varepsilon(a_1)a_2=a$, the displayed expression is exactly $D_i(a)b+(-1)^{d_i\deg a}aD_i(b)$. Expansion into simple tensors is legitimate because they span the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text: The other counit identity gives $\varepsilon(D_i(a))=\sum\phi_i(a_1)\varepsilon(a_2)=\phi_i(a)$. Set $a_{ij}=D_i(x_j)\in A^{d_j-d_i}$. When $d_j<d_i$ this is zero. When $d_j=d_i$ it is scalar, hence $a_{ij}=\varepsilon(D_i(x_j))1=\delta_{ij}1$. Thus the evaluation matrix has identity blocks in equal degrees and can have additional entries only when the column degree is strictly larger than the row degree. These additional entries need not vanish.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text:
For the normalization, check explicitly how a homogeneous coefficient changes the degree of a derivation. If $E$ has degree $-e$ and obeys the signed rule, and $h\in A^{e-d}$ with $e\geq d$, signed commutation gives, for homogeneous $a,b$,
$$hE(ab)=hE(a)b+(-1)^{e\deg a}haE(b)=hE(a)b+(-1)^{d\deg a}ahE(b),$$
because $ha=(-1)^{(e-d)\deg a}ah$ and $e+(e-d)\equiv d\pmod2$. Hence $hE$ is a linear derivation of degree $-d$, vanishing on $1$. Finite sums or differences with this same degree preserve these identities term by term. This calculation also holds in characteristic $2$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text:
Recursively over the finitely many generator degrees in decreasing order, define
$$\partial_i=D_i-\sum_{j:\,d_j>d_i}a_{ij}\partial_j.$$
At the greatest generator degree the sum is empty, so $\partial_i=D_i$. At any subsequent degree all maps in the sum have already been defined. Each $a_{ij}$ has degree $d_j-d_i$; the preceding coefficient calculation therefore shows that every summand has degree $-d_i$ and obeys the required signed rule. Thus $\partial_i$ is $k$-linear of degree $-d_i$, vanishes on $1$, and has the stated Leibniz identity. Generators of equal degree are defined simultaneously, with no dependence between them.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, Borel structure input, first sentence of proof; agent-written signed contraction and descending-normalization calculation, not asserted to be a proof printed in Milne.

proof.text: The same decreasing-degree induction verifies all generator values. Assume $\partial_j(x_l)=\delta_{jl}1$ for every $l$ whenever $d_j>d_i$. If $d_l>d_i$, evaluating the defining formula gives $\partial_i(x_l)=a_{il}-a_{il}=0$, because only the summand $j=l$ contributes. If $d_l\leq d_i$, every term in the sum evaluates to zero, and step 4 gives $\partial_i(x_l)=D_i(x_l)=\delta_{il}1$. The base case is step 4 for the greatest degree. This proves every claimed value and completes the construction. For $s=0$ there is no index $i$, so the assertion is vacuous. No step uses perfectness, cocommutativity, an antipode, or division by an integer.
